# Contribute a lab

## Curate an exhibit {#editable-curator .sa-exhibits}

### Choose

Check the source of the lab exercise.

### Place

Put the lab next to its prerequisites.

### Label

Use the page title to tell learners what they will measure.

::: {.callout-note}
A lab can belong in the course and still be hard to find.
:::

## Check the folder first {#editable-folder-check .sa-walkthrough sa-layout="accumulate"}

### Extract the submission {.sa-source}

Extract `branch-naming.zip` outside the repository.

- `conventions.md`
- `images/branch-map.svg`

### Run the dry run {.sa-command}

```sh
python3 scripts/contribution_to_qmd.py branch-naming --dry-run
```

### Inspect the report {.sa-result}

Check the proposed `conventions.qmd` and investigate missing links.

```{.yaml .number-lines}
output: conventions.qmd
warning: unresolved link to labs/branch-map
```

::: {.callout-note}
Read warnings as prompts to inspect the result.
:::

::: {.notes}
Pause after the dry run and ask what the warning tells us.
:::

## Preview and publish {#editable-publish .sa-mermaid-steps}

```{mermaid}
flowchart LR
  local["Local preview"] --> check["Check links"]
  check approved@-->|Verified| push["Push to main"]
  check --> stop["Fix and retry"]
```

1. [Build the local preview.]{sa-node="local"} Use the same inputs as the site.
2. [Check the links.]{sa-node="check"} Open them from the rendered page.
3. [Publish the verified change.]{sa-node="push" sa-edge="approved" sa-edge-label="approved"} Push to `main`.
4. [A broken link sends you back to editing.]{sa-node="stop" sa-from="check"} Rebuild the preview after fixing it.

## Predict the result {#editable-quiz .sa-quiz}

### What does a dry run change?

It reports the planned output. Review missing references against the [Mermaid documentation](https://mermaid.js.org/).

### How does reverse bias affect the depletion width?

For this illustrative model, $W \propto \sqrt{V_{bi} + V_R}$.

# Bias the junction

## Raise reverse bias {#editable-junction .sa-cues}

{{< include scenes/junction-figure.qmd >}}

### Increase the reverse bias {sa-cue="raise-bias"}

The depleted region widens. The curve shows an increase in peak field magnitude.

### Return to the starting bias {sa-cue="return-bias"}

The depletion width and field return to their starting values.
